name: Provider Data Mis-match — AND event on a DME claim: establish the member's state, then find the missing ordering NPI
description: Nine guided steps, one per row of the AND.1 document: identify the AND event among the claim's edits, confirm the place of service is 12 (Home), confirm the rendering provider's specialty is Durable Medical Equipment, confirm the procedure code is DME-related, read the subscriber's address to establish the member's state, check the Supporting Ordering NPI on the provider record, confirm the absence against field 44 of the claim image, deny with reject code PX_RANNPI, and submit the Deny decision.

steps.name: Identify the AND event
steps.description: Open the Event Resolution tab and look through the claim's edits for an AND event. The AND event means the claim may have been filed against the wrong plan: a Durable Medical Equipment claim belongs with the plan for the state where the equipment was sent or delivered, or where the retail store is located. The event alone does not tell you the answer. If the member's address turns out to be outside Our Insurance, the claim really was filed with the wrong plan and rejects with PX_RANDME; if the member is inside Our Insurance, the plan is right and something else is wrong with the claim. PX_AND is present here, so work through the claim and find out which.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes as soon as the trainee opens the Event Resolution tab.
steps.hint: Click the 'Event Resolution' tab. The Active Edit panel shows PX_AND — 'DME FILE TO STATE'. The All Edits list below shows it among the claim's other events.
steps.checklistItem: Event Resolution tab opened — PX_AND event identified

steps.name: Verify the Place of Service is 12 (Home)
steps.description: Review the place of service on the claim. Open the Claim Lines tab and read the POS field. Place of service 12 is Home — the equipment went to where the member lives, which is what makes the delivery address the thing that decides the plan. Here the POS is 12, so carry on.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes as soon as the trainee opens the Claim Lines tab.
steps.hint: Click the 'Claim Lines' tab and read the POS column on line 1. It reads 12 — Home.

steps.name: Verify the provider specialty is DME
steps.description: Review the provider's specialty to confirm this really is a Durable Medical Equipment claim. Open the Provider Information tab and read the Specialty Description field in the Rendering section. Here it reads V04 - DURABLE MEDICAL EQUIPMENT & MEDICAL SUPPLIES, so the AND event is being applied to the right kind of claim and you can carry on.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes as soon as the trainee opens the Provider Information tab.
steps.hint: Click the 'Provider Information' tab. In the Rendering section, 'Speciality description' reads V04 - DURABLE MEDICAL EQUIPMENT & MEDICAL SUPPLIES.
steps.checklistItem: Provider specialty confirmed as Durable Medical Equipment

steps.name: Verify the procedure code is DME-related
steps.description: Go back to the Claim Lines tab and read the procedure code. The specialty says the provider supplies durable medical equipment; the procedure code says what was actually billed. Here it is E0601, which is DME-related, so the claim is a DME claim on both counts and the AND event applies.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee RETURNS to the Claim Lines tab after this step activates. step_002 already visited that tab; the explicit variant records that this step is a deliberate return rather than a first visit. A visit-triggered step only ever completes while it is the active step, so the plain trigger would behave the same.
steps.hint: Click back to the 'Claim Lines' tab and read the Procedure column on line 1. It reads E0601.

steps.name: Verify the member address is within Our Insurance
steps.description: This is the step that decides the claim. Open the Member Information tab and read the Address field in the Subscriber section. The state in that address is the state the equipment was delivered to, and it determines which plan the claim belongs with. California is Our Insurance state, so this claim is filed with the right plan — the AND event's wrong-plan defect does not apply here, and PX_RANDME is not the answer. Because the plan is right, carry on and look for what else is wrong with the claim.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes as soon as the trainee opens the Member Information tab.
steps.hint: Click the 'Member Information' tab. In the Subscriber section, the Address field ends 'CA' — Our Insurance state, so the plan on the claim is correct.
steps.checklistItem: Member address confirmed within Our Insurance (CA)

steps.name: Check the ordering provider's NPI
steps.description: Go back to the Provider Information tab and find the ordering provider's NPI number in the Miscellaneous Data section, under Supporting ordering NPI. A DME claim has to say who ordered the equipment. Here the field carries no value, so no ordering NPI has been recorded against the claim.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee RETURNS to the Provider Information tab after this step activates. step_003 already visited that tab; the explicit variant records that this step is a deliberate return rather than a first visit. A visit-triggered step only ever completes while it is the active step, so the plain trigger would behave the same.
steps.hint: Click back to the 'Provider Information' tab and scroll to the Miscellaneous Data section. 'Supporting ordering NPI' is empty.
steps.checklistItem: Supporting ordering NPI checked — no value on the claim record

steps.name: Confirm no NPI on the claim image
steps.description: Confirm the absence against what the provider actually submitted. Open the Claim Image tab and find the Claim Image — Provider Information: Referring group, then read the Supporting field — field 44 of the claim form, 'Ordering NPI'. It has no value either, so the NPI is not missing from the record because somebody failed to key it: the provider never submitted one. In the real system this is the point at which you check the claim form itself.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes as soon as the trainee opens the Claim Image tab.
steps.hint: Click the 'Claim Image' tab. In 'Claim Image — Provider Information: Referring', the field labelled '44. Ordering NPI' is empty.
steps.checklistItem: Claim image field 44 confirmed empty — no ordering NPI submitted

steps.name: Deny the claim using Reject code PX_RANNPI
steps.description: The plan on the claim is correct, so the claim is not rejected for the plan. What is missing is the ordering provider's NPI, on the record and on the claim form alike, and that is what the claim is rejected for. From the Action menu select Deny claim. A Deny Claim section appears below the header. Enter reject code PX_RANNPI in the input box — the matching code appears in a dropdown list — select it and click Submit.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee submits the Deny Claim panel (which dispatches the deny_claim action).
steps.hint: Action menu → Deny claim. Enter reject code PX_RANNPI in the Deny Claim section, click Submit, then confirm the pop-up.
steps.checklistItem: Deny the claim using Reject code PX_RANNPI

steps.name: Submit Deny decision
steps.description: Finish the claim. In the Decision section of the claim summary header, select 'Deny' from the dropdown and click Submit.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the claim is submitted with the Deny decision selected. Submitting Pay does not complete it.
steps.hint: In the header's Decision dropdown pick 'Deny', then click Submit on the claim summary bar.
